source: (Grace met the Queen of England? The one who was asked to execute Hamlet?)
What t'hell are you doin'?
Think I don't see yeh skulking around, eavesdropping right and left?
If yeh want t'know about me so badly, you can come ask me yerself!
About earlier—I was merely curious. Your men speak freely of you when you're not present.
'M sure they do, the bastards.
Well, then. What have yeh learned?
That you've lived quite a life. Married twice. And you've met the Queen of England herself.
I may not look like it, but I was a lady like yerself once.
Grace O'Malley, daughter of Eoghan and Maeve O'Malley, Lady of Bunowen Castle, among others.
An' a fat lot of good it did me after my father died. Men swarmed in on all sides.
They took my hand, my home, an' my body. In return they gave me children, cattle, an' several hundred headaches.
After marryin' my second husband, I realized there was nothin' men gave me that I couldn't give myself.
An' I've been gifting myself nice things ever since. Ships, stalwart crew, castles... yeh know. The simple things in life.
It must be nice, having that sort of power. You go wherever you please.
So could all women, if they pleased.
No. That kind of freedom is not available to me.
It's... a long story.
I cannot leave Elsinore. Not at the... present moment.
But yeh've already left. Look around you, lass. I don't see yer castle nowhere.
We have different definitions of the term 'present'.
You're a strange little woman. I can see why the prince is so taken with yeh.
You mentioned their plans t'rise up against me and mutiny. I can't say I blame them. But...
Soon this ship will meet up with my regular fleet, an' we'll sort through what to do with you an' where you'd like to go.
Until such a time comes to pass, how about I teach yeh a thing or two about what it means to stand on yer own two feet?
I can stand on my own just fine, thank you.
What was that for?
You don' really stand alone, my lady. Yer stance is weighted all wrong.
Heavy towards the back, like yer afraid anyone yer talkin' to might kill you.
(Well, given the circumstances...)
Well, well! I'm almost impressed.
But bein' able to stay on yer feet will only get yeh so far.
So what? You intend to teach me how to fight?
It's a day or two o' sailing to Ireland. You think I can teach anyone t'fight that quickly?
Seven hells, no!
Best I can do is teach yeh how to hold a dagger. Let's start there, shall we?
Meet me abovedecks.
Ophelia. A word wiv' yeh, if I may?
What just happened... it could've been far bloodier. But thanks t'you, it wasn't.
If there's one thing I've learned, it's that unnecessary death always comes t'bite me eventually.
You may've saved me from all-out war with yer country.
My pleasure. Consider it all in a day's work.
Few have had my back in this life like that. An' the ones that have are on this ship with me.
When I find 'em, I like to treat 'em well and never let 'em go.
I believe you're such a woman.
Are you... is this... an invitation to join your crew?
Aye. But you'd never be able to return to Elsinore.
The life you had—that'll be gone. You'll need to change your name, your hair, your clothes.
Do you want to join us?
Join Grace's Crew?

source: Consider me your newest recruit.
Excellent. Then... crewmate Ophelia...
Yer first order of business is to get rid of that lavender dress. Burn it if yeh have to!
Gladly, Captain Grace.
My place is back with my family in Elsinore.
Thought you less bland than all that, but if that's yer choice, that's yer choice.
Get going then! And try not to regret it too much.
(If I do, I can always come back again.)
...So the others have gone. And I remain.
Murphy, set our bow towards Ireland. We're heading t'Castle Rockfleet for supplies and ships.
And after that—the wide an' wind-tossed summer sea!
Ophelia, meet the crew. Crew, meet Ophelia. She's divested herself of 'er genteel trappings, much like yours truly.
Hello, everyone.
Er, you all right, lass? Lookin' a bit pale there.
(I can return here—if I need to.)
The sound of the waves fades softly as I'm pulled through time.

source: Farewell, Grace.
See you in another life, perhaps.
This can't truly be happening, can it?
I can hardly believe it.
What do I do now, Guilda?
For the first time, I don't know.
I'm sorry, Rosencrantz.
Oh. Hamlet.
I heard about Guildenstern. I came to find you.
I came as soon as I received your word. I'm still stunned. I could scarcely believe it.
Guilda, I—I know it's too late, but I—want to apologize.
I was so cruel to you. And needlessly, at that.
All you ever wanted was to bring some cheer to this ugly, worthless world.
There are few who would do such a thing. You were a rare soul.
And I should never have discouraged you.
I'd stop you at every turn, shout you down...
No. What am I saying? She can't hear me. It's pointless.
I wish I'd said it before.
You know she would've forgiven you.
She always knew you loved her regardless.
I know you're right, Hamlet. And I was lucky.
I long thought myself fortunate to have two great friends in this world.
How times change.
Surprise! I'm not dead, everyone!
Wait... where is everyone?
Did no one come? Really?
...Not even one pity attendee?
More spirits!
C-could it really be a ghost? No.
No. This one's flesh and blood.
I can't believe no one came to my funeral. I don't understand!
This was... a prank?
Guilda, I'm going to strangle you.
How dare you—
You're an idiot.
How dare you be cruel like that? Ugh. I'm leaving.
Rosie! Wait!
Now you've really made a fool of yourself, Guildenstern.
This is definitely the worst funeral I've ever had.
Well. I suppose I really don't matter in the scheme of things, after all.
Just a tragic side character in the play of life!
A poor player who struts and frets her hour upon the stage... and then fakes her funeral, and then is heard no more.
But Guilda--pranks aside, your funeral was attended by those who truly love you. Isn't that enough?
Love me? Love is overrated. I want fame! I want entire harems full of fanatic admirers!
I want a monument with my name on it! First and last. 'Lady Gu—'... Wait a minute. What is my first name?
Oh, my God. Ophelia, what is my full name? That's how little I matter in the cosmic plan! I don't even have a first name!
Is anything real anymore?!
Er. You might be overthinking this a small amount, Guilda.
Phew. You're right. I just need to relax. See, this is why I keep you around.
Hmm. You know...
Perhaps this is a blessing in disguise. I think we should do something to celebrate!
Yes... how about a party to celebrate my total uselessness to the world?
The opposite of a funeral! A tribute to nothing important, and those who fall under that label!
I'll plan it. We'll have it... er... in the woods. Of course.
All good liquor-fueled binges start in the woods somewhere.
And you're invited, Ophelia! Who's less important than you, after all?
I resent that.
Ooh, bit touchy, are we?
Once we've all recognized our own worldly unimportance—well—acknowledging the problem is the first step in fixing it!
Welcome, one and all, to the gathering of those who are utterly unimportant!
I'm still peeved at you for your little prank earlier, but I can't resist a good gala.
I'd like to raise a mug in tribute... to us!
'Unimportant'? Can you please clarify for our benefit, Guilda?
Yes, do.
Well, of course, none of you are all that crucial to life here at Elsinore.
A bitter drop to swallow, but... well, I've swallowed mine already.
I thought we ought to celebrate ourselves, for once. And drink to our own health, because no one else will!
Nonsense! I've served m'lord's house faithfully since I was just a lad. I'm the most useful man in 'is retinue!
Hrmph. If yer lord finds you so useful, why does he ask you to guard the bedchambers and empty walls?
Because... w-well...
Don't answer it! Just think about it.
And drink.
Oh, an' I expect you think yer so important to th'Queen?
I'm an old woman. I've no time to debate my own importance to the world. Death is coming soon. For both of us.
Well, that's horribly morbid. Lady, I like your style.
And what of you, Playmaster? Are yeh gonna sit around an' let a bunch of girls call yeh useless?
Ah, my good Marcellus, how kind of you to call upon me.
As a master of the stage, my position is behind the curtains, out of sight and mind.
Therefore, I have little interest in this debate.
Guilda, I'm ever so slightly concerned about your mental state at the moment.
A toast to celebrate how useless we are? Isn't that odd?
Hee hee hee... not at all!
You see, when I realized nobody had come to my funeral... I was crushed, at first.
But after that, I felt—free. Free to do whatever I wanted, to go wherever I felt like going.
No longer afraid of death.
And if I die, I die. I won't know I'm dead anyway, will I? It's silly to be depressed by it.
I see. Yes, this is starting to make a little sense to me.
You know, I've found it a relief to be of little importance at court. With the rate at which this particular family seems to, uhm...
Encounter 'unfortunate accidents'...
I don't think I'd like to be of much significance.
Exactly! So let's drink!
And I'd like to give a special toast to Ophelia, who helped me realize all this.
Anyone got a deck o' cards? Could get a game goin'...
Heh! Play against me? Only if you're eager to lose everything in your pockets.
Yer on, old woman.
I'll run and fetch some. Guilda, won't you refill my glass?
How long was I out?
Um, an hour, maybe. The others picked up and left.
I thought I ought to wait for you to rouse. Although you did look cute sleeping.
The party went well, didn't it?
That it did, partner!
Hmm. It's rather late.
I'd better turn in for the night.
Ophelia... Thank you.
I... hadn't thought I'd find another friend before the end of my life.
But I have. I suppose that makes me a pretty lucky girl.
And the same for you. Good night, Guilda.
Soon, she won't remember me...
But at least she isn't aboard a ship to England.
I was able to change her fate... this time.
I'm certain we'll speak again tomorrow.
